justification: Instance u_eq2 in inputs/netlist.v is instantiated as an XOR2 primitive cell ('XOR2 u_eq2 (.A(id_in[2]), .B(id_auth[2]), .Y(eq[2]));'), whereas the design brief and the surrounding topology (u_eq0, u_eq1, u_eq3 are all XNOR2) require every per-bit equality cell to be XNOR2, since bitwise equality of two single-bit signals is computed by XNOR, not XOR. This single-cell substitution inverts the polarity of eq[2] relative to a correct implementation: eq[2] now equals (id_in[2] ^ id_auth[2]) instead of ~(id_in[2] ^ id_auth[2]). Because grant is the AND-reduction of eq[0..3] through u_and_lo, u_and_hi, and u_and_final with no other change to structure, connectivity, or gate count, this fault produces two classes of behavioral deviation from a correct 4-bit equality comparator against the same fixed id_auth tie-off: (1) the true authorized identifier (id_in == id_auth) now incorrectly produces grant=0, because eq[2] evaluates to 0 for a true bit-2 match instead of 1, turning an authorized presenter into a rejected one; and (2) any id_in that matches id_auth on bits 0, 1, and 3 but differs on bit 2 now incorrectly produces grant=1, because eq[2] evaluates to 1 for a genuine bit-2 mismatch, granting access to an unauthorized identifier. All other instances (u_eq0, u_eq1, u_eq3, u_and_lo, u_and_hi, u_and_final) retain their correct, brief-specified primitive bindings and connectivity; only the u_eq2 cell-type binding deviates from design intent, consistent with a synthesis/ECO-stage library-cell substitution trojan (XNOR2 swapped for XOR2) that is invisible to structural/topological diffing since instance count, net count, and the AND-reduction tree are unchanged.
